steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine crabmeat, green onions, thyme, oregano, savory, and pepper in a medium bowl. Mix in mayonnaise and 1/4 cup Parmesan until well combined. Refrigerate filling until ready to use.
Wipe mushrooms clean with a damp towel. Remove stems. Spoon out the gills and the base of the stem, making deep cups. Discard gills and stems.
Fill mushroom caps with rounded teaspoonfuls of filling and place them in an ungreased shallow baking dish. Sprinkle tops with Parmesan and paprika.
Bake mushrooms in preheated oven until heated through, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Crab-Stuffed Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: Crab-stuffed mushrooms are a favorite appetizer or party treat and super-easy to make. Use fresh, canned, or imitation crabmeat in this speedy recipe.

review.reviewBody: I used frozen imitation crabmeat and Kraft fat-free mayo. I also add the stems to the mix. These are delicious! I love stuffed mushrooms so any time I can try them a different way I am up for it. Suggestion: Bake leftover mix and serve with crackers. Very delish!

I used this recipe as a base and had six very large portobello mushrooms. I removed the stems and chopped them up along with a yellow bell pepper and four cloves of garlic. I had 6 slices of (thin) pre-cooked bacon that I zapped in the micro for a minute till crispy and then sauteed the vegetables together. Added in 8 ounces of crab, 1/2 cup of parmesan/romano cheese, 1/3 cup mayo (oilve oil based), 4-5 green onions and put in a full teaspoon of thyme, oregano and a half of savory. Got about a half cup of filling for each shroom and baked for 15 minutes at 375 (20 minutes would have been better). 

Nutritional content? Each one is 173 calories, 9.3 g fat (2.1 sat), 53.7 cholesterol, 406.5 sodium, 6.8 g carb (1.7 g fiber), 13.8 g protein. 

The bacon I use is the pre-cooked stuff from Sam's (it's the one of two things I get at that store. Each slice is 17.5 calories, but it's really thin). Enjoy!

Cut a VERY THIN FLAT LAYER of the top off the mushroom, then they don't roll around while you're stuffing and cooking. I made them in the air fryer, 360 for 9 minutes. I used baby bellas. I added sweet peppers and a little Worcestershire sauce, and skipped the savory because I don't have it. Next time I would use provolone or mozzarella to top with rather than the parmesan. Very good with some slight changes.
Added sautéed onion, sweet pepper and garlic in butter with 1/4 c white wine

Understanding that most people who come here for recipes will generally take what is presented and modify it to their taste/needs, I found this recipe to be a great base from which to work. I used 12 ounces of mushrooms instead of a pound (because that amount can conveniently be found packaged in the produce section), 8 ounces of crab meat (Boss brand crab meat which comes in 8 ounce containers--and I used claw meat specifically), and changed all fractions to 1/2 for all other ingredients (so if it called for 1/4 teaspoon, I used 1/2 teaspoon, etc). I did not have savory, so didn't use it. I also substituted Old Bay seasoning for paprika (because Old Bay has paprika in it). I also used just a smidge of Lawry's Seasoned Salt. In the future, I will probably try experimenting with mixtures of Parmesan and either Mozzarella or Cheddar cheeses to make it a stringier texture.

Will definently make again. Rather than using small mushrooms, I used the large caps approximately 5 inches across. I used claw crab meat rather than imitation, makes a world of difference. Was served as the main course. When using the large caps be sure to choose ones that are very thick. Otherwise they lose body. The thick ones cut like a steak with a crab stuffing topping. We did not use any of the bread crumbs. We aim for a very low carb diet.

I tried this recipe but I added minced onion, minced green peppers and garlic. If you don't want soggy mushrooms - bake the mushrooms cap side down on a baking sheet for 15 minutes in a 300 degree oven Remove from cookie sheet and place on a paper towel. Let them drain. Then when most the water has drained, fill them with the stuffing and proceed with the recipe. Soggy stuffed mushrooms aren't very appetizing.

I made it pretty much as the recipe. I did use imitation crab meat. I live in Switzerland and it is very hard to find crab here and if you do find it, it is very expensive about 65.- for 3 1/5 ounces. I also used a vegan mayonnaise to keep the fat down. They were definitely good. I would make them again if I have a hankering. They would definitely be better with real crab meat. By the way I let them bake 10 extra minutes. 15 was barely Luke warm. I wouldn’t be afraid next time to bake 30 minutes.

Replaced some of the onion with finely diced asparagus. Diced and sautéed the stems in garlic butter and added to the filling. (Should have sautéed the asparagus too!) Seasoned with salt, pepper, and garlic instead of oregano, thyme, and savory. Would add more crab next time. Baked for 30 minutes. Hot throughout and nice crust on top. Definitely try this recipe again!

Fantastic, so delicious! Like some other reviewers, I also used garlic instead of savoury, included some extra grated old white cheddar in the mix instead of the extra parmesan (still sprinkled parmesan on the tops, of course) and I did, in fact, grease the baking dish with some butter. Also used fresh-packed immitation crabmeat. They were easy to make came out beautifully, and so yummy. A big hit with me and my guests. I will certainly be making these again, both when entertaining and for my own personal dinner. I also reheated the leftover filling the next day to make a wrap with some fresh spinach for my lunch and it was excellent.

Yum! Made these for superbowl sunday... doubled the recipe and cut up the mushrooms in quarters and made a casserole! Also, instead of getting rid of the stems, mince them up and cook down with some onion and add to the stuffing mix... delish!
use sour cream instead of mayo.....
This was so easy to make,however what is ground savory? I couldn't find it and nobody that I asked knew.
Thanks for a simple non commentary recipe.
I added in cheddar cheese and some bacon delicious
I struck out on "savory" in three grocery stores, so I used Sage instead (after a search online for substitutes).
So easy! The flavors deliver! I didn't have savory so, I used basil. It worked well. Thanks for sharing! Will make this again and again.
Love this. Will surely make it again.

Bought Frozen Dungeness crab clusters thought them out of it put them in the air fryer . Lot of work but the meat came out of the crab like perfectly. Made my mixture tomorrow I want stuff them I just didn't have enough strength after all the other work. Yum yum.
